title: Comms Failover — Ethernet loss fails the PV over to cellular
preface: This test is to confirm the PV fails over from its Ethernet (primary) to cellular (secondary/backup) communication channel when Ethernet fails, continues validating normally on cellular, and fails back to Ethernet once Ethernet is restored.
preconds:
**GIVEN** a PV in service with Ethernet configured as the primary comms channel and cellular configured as the secondary/backup channel
**AND** a valid smartcard is available to present
**AND** you can verify the CloudFare Activity Log for the PrimaryCommsChannelFailed (event 812) set/clear entries

steps.expected:
**THEN** a PrimaryCommsChannelFailed (812) set event is raised in the CloudFare Activity Log
**AND** the PV fails over to the cellular connection

steps.content: **WHEN** the operator presents the smartcard to the PV while it is running on cellular
steps.expected:
**THEN** the 'Validation Success' screen is displayed
**AND** the transaction is identifiable in the back office (CloudFare, SmarTrack, MERIT)

**THEN** a PrimaryCommsChannelFailed (812) clear event is raised in the CloudFare Activity Log
**AND** the PV fails back to operating over Ethernet

citations: REQ-2746.0 (old suite 10047, C2700890 'Secondary Communication Failover Method' — NIR route, and C3275939 — Glider route): PV continues to operate as normal on cellular after Ethernet fails; transaction identifiable in CloudFare/SmarTrack/Merit/Merit Web Reporter

TIBU-24428 (PrimaryCommsChannelFailed event-spamming fix) — final Jira comment history: build 1.1.1151.27197 (2026-01-30, QA PASSED) confirms 'PrimaryCommsChannelFailed Event 812 (Set) raised when disconnecting ethernet... device then failed over to cellular' and 'Event 812 (Clear) raised after reconnecting the ethernet cable'; build 1.0.9603.23768 (2026-04-20, QA PASSED) confirms the full bidirectional matrix (Ethernet+Cellular connected → disconnect Ethernet → fails over to cellular → reconnect Ethernet → fails back)

gap-register.md Q23 (ANSWERED, George 2026-07-21: 'if there is an old test case with it, assume it has failover, for now') — reverses Q9's earlier 'Ethernet-only, no failover' answer for this specific case
change_note: RESTORED (George, 2026-07-21, second directive same day): this case was condemned earlier today (`ZZ_DELETE_REVIEW` prefix, gap-register Q9: 'PV is Ethernet-only, no failover') based on FBD-100359's Ethernet-device hard-failure rule. A later coverage-audit pass the same session found the OLD suite (10047, read-only) holds two real, populated REQ-2746.0 cases (C2700890, C3275939) that explicitly test the PV failing over to cellular and continuing to operate — directly contradicting the condemnation. This was logged as gap-register Q23 without being resolved. George has now ruled: assume the PV has real cellular failover, grounded on the old suite's REQ-2746.0 case content. Cross-checking TIBU-24428 (the ticket a previous pass cited as evidence AGAINST failover, quoting its bug-report preamble 'PV should continue to communicate over ethernet AND not fail over to cellular') against the FULL ticket history (not just the initial bug description) shows that quoted line was the INITIAL bug report's description of a *spurious/spamming* failover on a healthy Ethernet link — not a statement that failover doesn't exist. The ticket's own final QA-passed builds (1.1.1151.27197, then 1.0.9603.23768) explicitly implement and verify full bidirectional Ethernet⇌cellular failover with a named audit event (PrimaryCommsChannelFailed, 812, set/clear). So TIBU-24428 is not a counter-signal to REQ-2746.0 — read in full it corroborates it. Title reverted from `ZZ_DELETE_REVIEW - PV to BOS — communications resilience and failover`; body fully reworded (not just un-prefixed) to ground the mechanism precisely on REQ-2746.0 (continues to operate on cellular, transaction identifiable in back office) and TIBU-24428 (the named 812 set/clear event, the reconnect/fail-back behaviour) rather than the prior generic 'secondary failover channel' wording, and tightened from a 3-different-behaviour case into one aligned Ethernet-loss→cellular→Ethernet-restore scenario per the Gherkin standard's step-cap guidance. This does not duplicate sibling C4103568/C4103569, which now model the (rarer) both-channels-down hard-failure case, not single-channel failover.
gaps: FBD-100359 classifies 'Platform & Gate Validators' as an Ethernet-only device type with no cellular failover path described — this appears to be an incomplete/outdated device classification given the PV's confirmed cellular failover hardware and behaviour (REQ-2746.0, TIBU-24428). Not corrected here (out of scope — FBD text is a separate confidential document); flagged as a candidate FBD-100359 update, POSSIBLE SPEC GAP, for the requirements owner. George's directive is to proceed on the assumption failover is real 'for now', pending that formal correction.

title: Comms Lock — a sustained loss of both Ethernet and cellular drives the PV out of service
preface: This test is to confirm a PV enters a communication-locked, out-of-service state only when BOTH its Ethernet (primary) and cellular (secondary/backup) comms channels are lost for a sustained period — a single-channel Ethernet failure alone fails over to cellular and does not trigger this state (see 'Comms Failover').
preconds:
**GIVEN** a PV in service with Ethernet as the primary comms channel and cellular as the secondary/backup channel
**AND** both the Ethernet and cellular connections are lost and stay down together for a significant period

steps.content: **WHEN** the loss of both channels is sustained beyond the device's offline tolerance
steps.expected:
**THEN** the PV enters a communication-locked, out-of-service state
**AND** the PV stops accepting taps

citations: FBD-100359 (hard-failure rule: on a sustained Translink-network outage, Ethernet devices operate offline, then after a significant period may enter a communication-locked out-of-service state)

TIBU-24428 — QA-passed test-coverage matrix (Thomas James, 2026-04-20, build 1.0.9603.23768): the only scenario producing 'Device has not back-office connection' is 'Ethernet & Cellular not connected'; every single-channel-down scenario in the same matrix instead fails over to the surviving channel and keeps the PV in service
change_note: NARROWED (reconciled against the restore of sibling C4101085 this session). As written, this case's precondition/steps read as if any sustained loss of the Translink-network Ethernet path alone — regardless of cellular — drives the PV to the comms-locked, out-of-service state. That is now understood to be incomplete: REQ-2746.0 (old suite) and TIBU-24428's own final QA-passed test-coverage matrix both confirm a single Ethernet-channel failure fails over to cellular and keeps the PV operating normally; TIBU-24428's matrix explicitly separates 'Ethernet & Cellular not connected' (no back-office connection) from every single-channel-down case (fails over, stays in service). This case is narrowed to the correct, more specific trigger — sustained loss of BOTH channels together — rather than describing the general FBD-100359 Ethernet-device hard-failure rule as if the PV had no cellular backup at all. No behaviour is invented: the both-channels-down trigger and its out-of-service/no-taps outcome are unchanged from the FBD-100359 text; only the precondition is narrowed to reflect that the PV specifically has a cellular failover path FBD-100359's device list doesn't call out.
gaps: FBD-100359 does not itself distinguish 'Ethernet-only sustained outage' from 'both channels down' for the PV — that distinction is drawn here from TIBU-24428's test evidence, not from a corrected FBD-100359 text. Recommend FBD-100359 be annotated/updated to reflect the PV's actual cellular-failover architecture (same note as the gap logged against C4101085).
